newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish debt yields end down on foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Swedish debt yields end down on foreign markets.

text.p: Swedish debt yields fell sharply at the opening on Monday in the wake of lower yields overseas and remained lower through the day.
By the close the nine year bond yield was nine basis points lower at 6.67 percent.
"But we have spread apart somewhat from Germany on long yields," one dealer said. The German-Swedish gap increased by three basis points to 84.
Six month T-bill rates dropped four basis points to 3.69 percent.
Dealers said the focus was U.S. December CPI due Tuesday.
Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, will announce its weekly repo operation 0830 GMT on Tuesday but most dealers were not expecting any change in the repo rate from 4.10 percent.
"I think the Riksbank wants to see more statistics before lowering. It will want to see the CPI figures that are due on January 21," one dealer said.
The crown ended at 4.3560 to the mark, which was stronger 4.3570 in late trade Friday but lower than afternoon levels.
"We saw some Swedish industrial companies buying currency for crowns. But I think the crown will keep its strength," one dealer said. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
